comments.author: Keyframe
comments.story: Source code for 4kb demoscene production “Elevated” released
comments.why: Demo that inspired a career in graphics programming
comments.text: Second Reality was the best. First demo that I saw was Spaceballs' State of the art [LINK] and I vividly remember of thinking 'wtf is that, a video or what?' and then Second Reality a year later or so - [LINK] But then (I look all and every demo out there by then at the age of 13) I saw Mars demo [VIDEO] which hooked me forever on the path of graphics programming.

comments.author: reconnecting
comments.story: MacPaint Art from the Mid-80s Still Looks Great Today
comments.why: 6KB terrain demo running at 30+ fps on a 286
comments.text: It's amazing what people achieved with the resources of the '80s, creating fairly enjoyable visuals using extremely limited technology. Another example from the early '90s is MARS.COM (1) by Tim Clarke (1993). Just 6 kilobytes and 30+ fps on a 12MHZ 286 (2). 1. [VIDEO] 2. [LINK]

comments.author: velosol
comments.story: Demoscene accepted as UNESCO cultural heritage in The Netherlands
comments.text: Thinking about demos brought me right back to probably one of the first things I downloaded, the 'controllable' Mars demo [1,2]. I zoomed around that landscape in the way a child can pour hours into what anyone older would view as painfully repetitive. comments.author: cousin_it
comments.why: Efficient 1993 terrain demo contrasted with slow modern CSS voxels
comments.text: Voxels are the most expensive way to model a 3D shape, and browser CSS is the slowest way to render a 3D shape. These two were made for each other. The next step is to reimplement the Mars DOS demo [1] using voxels in the browser, and marvel at the slowdown compared to 1993. It's discouraging that we're supposed to cheer for progress even when it's headed backwards. [1] [VIDEO]
